spec_match.rationale: Tools are registered with inputSchema/execute, discovered with getTools() and run with executeTool(tool, input, { signal }); the trace shows the real resolved JSON string or rejection. Code sample corrected to document.modelContext.

interactive.rationale: Seven scripted prompts, freestyle (Enter, IME-safe, and Send) and Reset all drive real calls; meters are <output>s.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb says the tool choice is a keyword stand-in for a model and the calls are real, which is what happens.

edge_cases.rationale: Checkout total now uses quantities (2+3 units -> 122.5). Covers a throwing execute (OperationError), input failing its inputSchema (not executed), an AbortSignal.timeout deadline (TimeoutError) and a no-match prompt.

references.rationale: Links the WebMCP spec, explainer and ChromeStatus; the stale WICG link is gone.

conformance.rationale: Unchanged suite (immutable). Flag on, all 6 assertions run against a real document.modelContext; flag off, every guarded assertion passes vacuously and registertool-rejects-tool-without-name passes only because document.modelContext is undefined. Needs a human decision; the page no longer contradicts the suite (it targets document.modelContext).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 driven by Node Playwright against the local server, with and without --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, at 360x740 DPR3 touch and 1280x800. chrome-devtools-mcp is not available in this cloud environment, so this is NOT DevTools-MCP verification (rule 7b) and no accessibility-tree dump was taken; DOM semantics (roles, aria-pressed, label.control, live regions) were checked by script. Flag on, the deliberate checkout-on-empty-cart path makes Chrome log "WebMCP tool execution failed" (browser-generated, documented on the page); otherwise 0 console errors, 0 failed requests, 0px overflow.

telemetry_health.rationale: The page now reports window.showcaseTelemetry.support("document.modelContext", supported|flag|unsupported) from its capability check, on top of the shared runtime error capture. No interaction events.

design_system.rationale: Uses design-system variables; the flag/OT banner matches the feature page.

accessibility.rationale: Visible associated label on the prompt, trace is role=log aria-live=polite and focusable, meters are labelled <output>s, Enter guarded with isComposing.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px overflow and all controls >= 44px tall at 360x740 DPR3; desktop unchanged.

openQuestions.title: Flag for a human: WebMCP conformance suite passes vacuously and asserts sync throw for a promise API
openQuestions.detail: Conformance is immutable, so this is a human decision. On Chromium 157 without the flag the suite reads 6/6 PASS with no document.modelContext; the 'throws' assertion for a nameless tool only passes because the property access throws. In the spec registerTool returns a Promise and a missing required dictionary member becomes a rejected promise (verified with the flag: the promise rejects with TypeError), so a synchronous-throw contract is the wrong shape. Additive assertions for getTools()/executeTool(), name-charset InvalidStateError, duplicate-name InvalidStateError and AbortSignal unregistration (all verified behaviourally on Chromium 157 + WebMCP flag) would make the suite meaningful.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify with chrome-devtools-mcp (Canary + WebMCP flag) and inspect the accessibility tree
openQuestions.detail: This pass used Playwright headless Chromium 157 because chrome-devtools-mcp was unavailable; repeat the control walk, console/network check and accessibility-tree inspection through the MCP per rule 7b.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live log region announcing appended status rows; toggle button aria-pressed
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use aria-pressed for toggle state, associate every <label> with its control via for/id, and announce dynamic results through one polite live region or <output>.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: role=status on the mode banner, role=log + aria-live=polite on traces, <output> for results and meters, aria-pressed on selectable buttons, for/id labels on generated fields.

guidanceConsulted.query: toggle button group with minimum touch target size; controls without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Size targets with min-block-size/min-inline-size from a --target-size token (24px, 44px under pointer: coarse) and let grid tracks shrink (minmax(0, 1fr)) so nothing overflows at 320-360px.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: --target-size token with @media (pointer: coarse) at 44px; minmax(0, …) tracks and min-inline-size: 0 on grid children. Measured 0px overflow and no control under 44px at 360x740.

summary: Fixed 2026-11-24: the page now uses the real WebMCP surface (document.modelContext registerTool/getTools/executeTool) when Chrome exposes it, and a labelled spec-shaped stand-in (v146/webmcp/webmcp-live.js) otherwise, with the flag and origin-trial steps on the page. Remaining gaps: the immutable conformance suite passes vacuously without the flag (human decision) and the run was not DevTools-MCP verified.
